guard_streams.source: Local Full Fibre Networks Programme wave one final evaluation
guard_streams.write_limit: Pilot-project evaluation findings and counterfactual analyses are historical programme evidence, not current selected-parcel availability.

facts.detail: The wave one final evaluation was published on 14 December 2023.
Ipsos UK was commissioned in May 2018 to evaluate wave one projects.
The evaluation covers four pilot projects.
The projects were West Sussex, Tameside, the Trans Pennine Initiative and Schools.
A synthesis report provides an overview of the wave one projects.
Separate project reports provide more detailed project-level findings.
The evaluation includes counterfactual analysis of connectivity and economic impacts.
It includes qualitative findings.
It assesses evidence on public-sector impacts.
A technical annex documents the analytical approach.

guard_streams.source: Superfast Broadband Programme Evaluation: Key Benefits and Impacts
guard_streams.write_limit: Historical evaluation of programme benefits, productivity and value for money cannot verify current orderability or measured speed for selected parcels.

facts.detail: The key benefits and impacts report was published on 11 March 2025.
The Superfast Broadband programme was announced in 2010.
The programme responded to concerns that commercial rollout would not reach many areas.
BDUK is the accountable body for the programme.
The final evaluation round focused on phase three delivery.
The evaluation asks what outcomes the programme produced.
It examines behavioural changes associated with those outcomes.
It evaluates effectiveness and efficiency of delivery.
It assesses whether the investment was cost effective.
It identifies lessons for future policy design and implementation.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Rural Gigabit Connectivity Hubs Evaluation
guard_streams.write_limit: Evaluation evidence around connected public buildings and nearby outcomes cannot establish current selected-parcel serviceability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The Rural Gigabit Connectivity Hubs evaluation was published on 14 December 2023.
The evaluated Rural Gigabit Connectivity programme ran from 2019 to 2022.
The intervention connected remote public buildings such as schools and GP surgeries.
The report reviews impacts by the end of 2022.
The evaluation found evidence of increased broadband availability and uptake around Hubs.
Surveys found high satisfaction among connected schools.
Schools reported increased use of internet and educational technologies.
Awareness of Hub investments among nearby residents was relatively low.
There was some evidence of community-led take-up schemes near Hubs.
Nearby businesses reported benefits including adoption of new sales methods.
